req.title: Task description accepts long text
req.statement: The system shall accept task descriptions up to at least 1000 characters.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-032 requires the system to accept task descriptions up to at least 1000 characters. However, inspection of app/schemas.py reveals that TaskBase.description has max_length=500, meaning the schema will reject descriptions longer than 500 characters with a 422 Unprocessable Entity. The tests must cover: (1) a positive case with a description well within the schema limit (EP), (2) a boundary case at exactly the schema's declared max_length=500 (BVA — the actual enforced boundary), (3) a boundary case at 501 characters which the schema rejects (BVA + NEG — catches off-by-one mutations on the max_length constant), (4) a negative case with an empty/null description to confirm optional field handling (NEG), and (5) a case at exactly 1000 characters to directly probe the stated requirement boundary — this will expose the schema defect (BVA against requirement). All tests use in-process FastAPI TestClient with exact status code assertions and exact response field assertions to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.executable:
import os, sys
os.environ.setdefault('DATABASE_URL', 'sqlite:///./test_r032_ep.db')
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app
from app import models
from app.database import engine
models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
client = TestClient(app)
desc_100 = 'A' * 100
payload = {'title': 'Long Desc Task', 'description': desc_100, 'completed': False}
def test_create_task_description_typical_length_accepted():
    r = client.post('/tasks/', json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert body['description'] == desc_100
    assert body['title'] == 'Long Desc Task'
    assert body['completed'] == False
    assert 'id' in body
test_create_task_description_typical_length_accepted()
